column2: Rowstore storage groups data by {{c1::row}} rather than by column.
column3:
Putting the columns of one row together suits queries that fetch several fields for a single record. Columnstore groups the same column across rows instead.
Review source

column2: Disk-based rowstore indexes use a {{c1::B+ tree}} structure.
column3:
The upper levels direct a search toward the leaf pages. They let a seek avoid reading every leaf when it needs only a small range.
Review source

column2: A SQL Server table can have at most {{c1::one}} clustered index.
column3:
A clustered structure is the table's primary storage. Add nonclustered indexes when the same table needs additional access paths.
Review source

column2: A disk-based rowstore table without a clustered index is a {{c1::heap}}.
column3:
A heap lacks clustered key order. Its nonclustered indexes use a row identifier rather than a clustered key to locate data.
Review source

column2: On a clustered rowstore table, a nonclustered index uses the {{c1::clustered index key}} as its row locator.
column3:
The clustered key identifies the data row for a lookup. On a heap, the locator instead points to the row's storage location.
Review source

column2: In a nonclustered rowstore index, included columns appear only at the {{c1::leaf}} level.
column3:
Included values sit with the leaf entries and can supply the query output. They do not act as search or sort keys.
Review source

column2: To create a clustered rowstore index, use CREATE {{c1::CLUSTERED}} INDEX IX_Product_ID ON dbo.Product(ProductID);
column3:
This statement makes ProductID the clustered storage key. If the table already has a clustered index, it cannot have a second one.
Review source

column2: To create a nonclustered rowstore index, use CREATE {{c1::NONCLUSTERED}} INDEX IX_Product_Category ON dbo.Product(Category);
column3:
This creates a separate index to find rows by Category. The table keeps its existing primary storage structure.
Review source

column2: Add nonkey output columns with CREATE NONCLUSTERED INDEX IX_Product_Category ON dbo.Product(Category) {{c1::INCLUDE}} (ProductName, Price);
column3:
Category supports searches by category, while the two included fields can supply output without a lookup. The included fields do not extend the sort key.
Review source

column2: The data for one column within one columnstore rowgroup forms a {{c1::column segment}}.
column3:
Each compressed rowgroup has separate segments for its columns. A query can scan only the segments for the fields it needs.
Review source

column2: A full delta rowgroup normally closes at {{c1::1,048,576}} rows.
column3:
A full delta group stops accepting inserts at this size and can then be compressed. The separate bulk-load threshold is smaller.
Review source

column2: A bulk load usually needs at least {{c1::102,400}} rows in a batch per partition to bypass the clustered columnstore deltastore.
column3:
The threshold applies to rows going to each partition. For example, splitting 150,000 rows evenly across two partitions does not meet it in either partition.
Review source

column2: A delta rowgroup that still accepts new rows has state_desc = {{c1::OPEN}}.
column3:
An OPEN group still accepts rowstore inserts. Once it closes, new rows go elsewhere and the group waits for compression.
Review source

column2: A full delta rowgroup waiting for tuple-mover compression has state_desc = {{c1::CLOSED}}.
column3:
CLOSED means the delta group no longer accepts new rows. It remains in rowstore format until the engine compresses it.
Review source

column2: A rowgroup stored in compressed columnar format has state_desc = {{c1::COMPRESSED}}.
column3:
COMPRESSED identifies a rowgroup stored as column segments. OPEN and CLOSED instead describe stages in the deltastore.
Review source

column2: On an eligible heap table, create its primary columnstore storage with CREATE {{c1::CLUSTERED COLUMNSTORE}} INDEX CCI_Sales ON dbo.Sales;
column3:
This statement makes columnstore the table's primary storage. The engine includes the table's columns without a separate column list.
Review source

column2: Add a secondary columnstore copy with CREATE {{c1::NONCLUSTERED COLUMNSTORE}} INDEX NCCI_Sales ON dbo.Sales(Amount, Quantity);
column3:
The base table stays rowstore while the index stores the listed fields in columnar format. It can serve queries that aggregate Amount or Quantity.
Review source

column2: In sys.dm_db_column_store_row_group_physical_stats, {{c1::total_rows}} includes rows marked deleted in a compressed rowgroup.
column3:
The count includes stored rows that queries no longer return. Compare it with deleted_rows when estimating how much data the group still serves.
Review source

column2: In sys.dm_db_column_store_row_group_physical_stats, {{c1::deleted_rows}} counts rows marked for deletion within a compressed clustered columnstore rowgroup.
column3:
A marked row is hidden from normal results but can still take space. Compare deleted_rows with total_rows to see how much of a group is marked.
Review source

column2: In sys.dm_db_column_store_row_group_physical_stats, {{c1::size_in_bytes}} reports the combined page size for a rowgroup.
column3:
The reported bytes help compare how much space rowgroups occupy. The number does not include metadata or shared dictionaries.
Review source
